solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Idle brutes, if disturbed, played for time

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown out of order, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lazy thugs, once shaken up, stalled for time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges IDLE BRUTES IF. Filibustering is making long speeches in a legislature to delay a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: To filibuster is to obstruct proceedings by talking at length, deliberately using up the available hours.

clue.text: Female struggling to walk, an erstwhile lover?

explanation.surface: A woman hobbling along turns out to be someone's ex.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'old flame' is a former sweetheart, hence 'erstwhile'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flame is an idiomatic word for a sweetheart, most often used of a past romance.

clue.text: Left to help a team temporarily out of action?

parts.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Someone stayed behind to assist a squad that is sidelined for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: something laid aside is set down for now.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put away for the time being is no longer in use, pending a later return.

clue.text: Rely on New Testament as money-related document

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

indicators.note: New suggests a fresh version, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A believer trusts the New Testament like a financial record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Testament' reads as the Bible's second part; 'New' is the anagram signal turning TESTAMENT into STATEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed summary of an account's deposits and withdrawals is a financial paper from the lender.

clue.text: Sequence provided by street band

parts.note: a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A run of numbers is performed by a group of buskers.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of things is a series of them following one after another.

clue.text: Like issues raised by eco-warriors showing violent manner possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints that the preceding letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Green activists' concerns come across in an aggressive style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges VIOLENT MANNER; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eco-warriors campaign about pollution, climate and nature, the concerns of ecology.

clue.text: I've a radio — listener engaged there

indicators.note: the letters are held, engaged, within the run of words just before

explanation.surface: Someone owns a wireless and a listener is tuned in.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing is what does the listening, a common crossword equivalence.

clue.text: Top location in English Channel

definitions.meaning: a knitted pullover worn on the upper body
one of the Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy

explanation.surface: The best spot in the sea between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted pullover garment shares its name with the largest Channel Island.

clue.text: Strange article masking untruth

indicators.note: masking means covering up, so the first piece wraps around the second

explanation.surface: An odd piece of writing conceals a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means foreign or unfamiliar, hence odd.

clue.text: Minister of religion by lake in a state of abstraction

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric's title
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A clergyman sitting beside a lake is lost in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie is a daydream, a condition of being absorbed in thought.

clue.text: English artist in a particular period

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A British painter working in a certain age.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a distinct span of history marked by some feature.

clue.text: Senator is going out to see ladies abroad

indicators.note: going out suggests the letters are being disrupted from their order

explanation.surface: A politician heads off to visit women overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' rearranges SENATOR IS; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish speakers address unmarried women with this title, so they are ladies in a foreign land.

clue.text: So the soldiers must go over front

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means placed above, so the earlier pieces sit on top of the next

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

explanation.surface: The troops have to cross the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: So and the answer are both connectives meaning for that reason or consequently.

clue.text: Heather is a girl's name

definitions.meaning: the botanical genus of heaths and heathers

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather has a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The heath plant's Latin genus doubles as a feminine first name.

clue.text: One banqueting, not the first, in celebratory season

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a feaster is someone who banquets

explanation.surface: Someone is feasting during a festive time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian spring festival marking the Resurrection is a time of celebration.

clue.text: Poor journalist coming into money after turnabout

indicators.note: coming into means one piece enters the other
after a turnabout the word for money is read backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A hard-up reporter gets cash after a change of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal happens first, giving NEY, before 'coming into' inserts the journalist; 'turnabout' also hints at the surface's change of luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy and poor both describe people lacking enough to live on.

clue.text: Pole put up, fixed in English county

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is written upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A post erected and secured somewhere in the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses ROD to DOR. Dorset is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is one of the shires of south-west England, an example of the class.

clue.text: One handling goods in shop interrupted by woman and daughter

indicators.note: interrupted by means the first piece is broken open by what follows

explanation.surface: A shopworker is disturbed by a mother and her girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a docker who loads and unloads cargo from ships.

clue.text: Some yellow length of cloth

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A piece of yellow fabric measured off.
explanation.definitionFit: The ell is an old unit for measuring fabric, about 45 inches in England.

clue.text: Countries with pounds and shillings

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, abbreviates pounds
S abbreviates shillings, from Latin solidus; the shilling was a pre-decimal British coin

explanation.surface: Nations listed with their old currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Lands is a plain synonym for nations or territories.

clue.text: Quick to communicate

definitions.meaning: fast, as an ... train or delivery
to put into words, to convey a thought

explanation.surface: Eager to get a message across.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both speedy, as in a fast train, and to voice or convey a feeling.

clue.text: Author's short piece of verse

definitions.note: read as Author is, the 's being the link

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its end

parts.note: a poem is a piece of verse

explanation.surface: A writer's brief poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author's' reads as 'Author is'. Edgar Allan Poe was the American writer of tales and verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer, so the surname fits a generic writer.

clue.text: Old character — one's a bit prickly

definitions.meaning: a runic letter used in Old English for the th sound
a spike on a rose stem

explanation.surface: A grumpy old fellow who is somewhat touchy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an obsolete letter of the Old English alphabet and a sharp spine on a plant.

clue.text: Let's tolerate different people who don't touch alcohol

indicators.note: different means made otherwise, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to accept those who live differently, the abstainers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are abstainers who refuse all intoxicating drinks on principle.
